title: Assess wireless, cloud, and remote network architecture: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: For this wireless, cloud, edge, or remote path, who admits traffic, where is policy enforced, what provider/physical dependency remains, and how is loss or revocation handled?
focalInsight: Radio, provider, and programmable-network choices move trust boundaries; the service path must retain explicit identity, segmentation, visibility, and failure decisions.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Wireless Networks
nodes.definition: Networks using RF or other nonwired media with association, radio, physical-range, and interference considerations.
nodes.detail: Networks using RF or other nonwired media with association, radio, physical-range, and interference considerations.
nodes.decision: Select identity/admission, encryption, segmentation, management, rogue detection, and availability controls for the radio environment.
nodes.failureExample: An attacker associates from outside a facility because radio range and rogue monitoring were ignored.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Wireless design must cover association, radio exposure, and segmentation.

nodes.label: Wifi
nodes.definition: IEEE 802.11 wireless LAN technology using access points and association/security mechanisms.
nodes.detail: IEEE 802.11 wireless LAN technology using access points and association/security mechanisms.
nodes.decision: Use strong enterprise admission where needed, separate guest/IoT/enterprise traffic, secure AP management, and monitor rogue associations.
nodes.failureExample: Guest Wi-Fi shares routes with payroll systems through a flat wireless VLAN.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Wi-Fi security includes client admission and path separation.

nodes.label: Bluetooth
nodes.definition: Short-range wireless technology for peripheral/device communication with pairing and proximity risks.
nodes.detail: Short-range wireless technology for peripheral/device communication with pairing and proximity risks.
nodes.decision: Allow only needed profiles/devices, manage pairing, update firmware, and consider discovery/range exposure.
nodes.failureExample: An unmanaged paired device receives data after the authorized user leaves.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Bluetooth risk centers on pairing, device identity, and proximity.

nodes.label: Zigbee
nodes.definition: Low-power mesh wireless technology common in IoT, with coordinator/mesh and device-lifecycle dependencies.
nodes.detail: Low-power mesh wireless technology common in IoT, with coordinator/mesh and device-lifecycle dependencies.
nodes.decision: Segment IoT, manage commissioning/keys/firmware, and monitor gateway/control points.
nodes.failureExample: A compromised sensor joins a flat enterprise path through an unprotected gateway.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Zigbee needs IoT admission and gateway segmentation.

nodes.label: Cellular 4g 5g
nodes.definition: Provider-operated mobile access networks with SIM/device identity, radio coverage, carrier, and roaming dependencies.
nodes.detail: Provider-operated mobile access networks with SIM/device identity, radio coverage, carrier, and roaming dependencies.
nodes.decision: Assess carrier trust, device identity, private/public path, data exposure, coverage/fallback, and management.
nodes.failureExample: Loss of carrier service disables a remote safety function with no fallback.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Cellular availability and provider dependency are design inputs.

nodes.label: Satellite
nodes.definition: Long-distance radio communication via satellite with coverage, provider, latency, weather, and ground-station dependencies.
nodes.detail: Long-distance radio communication via satellite with coverage, provider, latency, weather, and ground-station dependencies.
nodes.decision: Use when geographic reach justifies latency/cost; plan encryption endpoints, provider trust, availability, and alternate paths.
nodes.failureExample: A latency-sensitive control service fails because satellite delay/jitter was not modeled.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Satellite expands reach but changes latency and dependency assumptions.

nodes.label: Remote Connectivity
nodes.definition: Controlled connectivity for offsite users/devices/services to organization resources.
nodes.detail: Controlled connectivity for offsite users/devices/services to organization resources.
nodes.decision: Broker identity, MFA, device posture, least privilege, time bounds, logging, revocation, and approved paths.
nodes.failureExample: A remote VPN user inherits broad internal routing after authentication.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Remote connectivity must constrain session identity, device, scope, and time.

nodes.label: Edge Network
nodes.definition: Compute/enforcement close to users/devices that can reduce latency but distributes trust and management.
nodes.detail: Compute/enforcement close to users/devices that can reduce latency but distributes trust and management.
nodes.decision: Define edge identity, configuration, data path, update/rollback, telemetry, and physical/provider ownership.
nodes.failureExample: An unpatched edge node enforces stale policy close to many clients.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Edge shifts control closer; it also distributes management risk.

nodes.label: Cdn
nodes.definition: Origin-and-edge distribution service that caches/delivers content through provider-operated edge nodes.
nodes.detail: Origin-and-edge distribution service that caches/delivers content through provider-operated edge nodes.
nodes.decision: Define origin trust, cache rules, TLS termination, invalidation, logging, data sensitivity, and provider failure behavior.
nodes.failureExample: Sensitive personalized content is cached or logged at an edge contrary to policy.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: CDN design starts with what may be cached and where TLS terminates.
